title: Rama breaks Shiva's bow
introduction: Rama breaks Shiva's bow when he wanted to examine the tautness of its bowstring. Janaka is perplexed, while others swooned at the blast of breaking bow, and Janaka proposes Seetha to Rama in marriage. On the approval of Vishvamitra to that proposal, Janaka sends his plenipotentiaries to Ayodhya.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 67th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
जनकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः |
धनुर्दर्शय रामाय इति होवाच पार्थिवम्
verses.iast:
janakasya vacaḥ śrutvā viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ |
dhanur darśaya rāmāya iti ha uvāca pārthivam
verses.translation: On listening to the words of Janaka, the eminent-saint Vishvamitra indeed said to the king Janaka thus as, "let the bow be displayed to Rama..."

glosses.meaning: to Rama, bow, may be shown

verses.devanagari:
ततः स राजा जनकः सचिवान् व्यादिदेश ह |
धनुरानीयतां दिव्यं गन्धमाल्यानुलेपितम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ sa rājā janakaḥ sacivān vyādideśa ha |
dhanur ānīyatām divyam gandha mālya anulepitam
verses.translation: Then king Janaka indeed ordered his ministers, "bring the divine bow which is decorated with sandalwood paste and garlands...

glosses.meaning: with sandalwood paste, garlands, bedaubed - decorated with

verses.devanagari:
जनकेन समादिष्ठाः सचिवाः प्राविशन् पुरम् |
तद्धनुः पुरतः कृत्वा निर्जग्मुरमितौजसः
नृणां शतानि पंचाशद्व्यायतानां महात्मनाम् |
मंजूषामष्टचक्रां तां समूहुस्ते कथंचन
verses.iast:
janakena samādiṣṭhāḥ sacivāḥ prāviśan puram |
tat dhanuḥ purataḥ kṛtvā nirjagmuḥ amita aujasaḥ
nṛṇām śatāni pañcāśat vyāyatānām mahātmanām |
mañjūṣām aṣṭa cakrām tām samūhuḥ te kathañcana
verses.translation: Thus clearly instructed by Janaka those high souled ministers have gone out from there and entered the palace-chambers, and they came out with an eight-wheeled coffer in which the bow of Shiva is ensconced, and those ministers got it tugged by five thousand tall men of illimitable energy who somehow tugged it very difficultly, and thus the ministers have re-entered there keeping that bow afore of them.

glosses.meaning: not, limitable, energetic ones [wheel cart pullers, not ministers]

verses.devanagari:
तामादाय तु मंजूषामायसीं यत्र तद्धनुः |
सुरोपमं ते जनकमूचुर्नृपतिमन्त्रिणः
verses.iast:
tām ādāya tu mañjūṣām āyasīm yatra tat dhanuḥ |
suropamam te janakam ūcuḥ nṛpati mantriṇaḥ
verses.translation: On fetching that iron coffer wherein that bow is there, those ministers of the king have reported to their godlike King Janaka.

glosses.meaning: to god, in simile [like,] Janaka, they said.

verses.devanagari:
इदं धनुर्वरं राजन् पूजितं सर्वराजभिः |
मिथिलाधिप राजेन्द्र दर्शनीयं यदिच्छसि
verses.iast:
idam dhanur varam rājan pūjitam sarva rājabhiḥ |
mithilā adhipa rāja indra darśanīyam yat icchasi
verses.translation: "Oh king and sovereign of Mithila, here is the select bow that is reverenced by all kings, oh, best king, which you wished to be evincible to the boys, to evince their capabilities...

glosses.meaning: which, evincible, you wished to - such a bow

verses.devanagari:
तेषां नृपो वचः श्रुत्वा कृताञ्जलिरभाषत |
विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
verses.iast:
teṣām nṛpo vacaḥ śrutvā kṛta añjaliḥ abhāṣata |
viśvāmitram mahātmānam tau ubhau rāma lakṣmaṇau
verses.translation: On listening the announcement of his ministers the king spoke to the noble souled Vishvamitra and to both Rama and Lakshmana too duly making palm-fold.

glosses.meaning: their [of his ministers,] words, on listening
to them, both, Rama, Lakshmana[ abhaaSata = spoke to.

verses.devanagari:
इदं धनुर्वरं ब्रह्मन् जनकैरभिपूजितम् |
राजभिश्च महावीर्यैरशक्तैः पूरितं तदा
verses.iast:
idam dhanur varam brahman janakaiḥ abhipūjitam |
rājabhiḥ ca mahā vīryaiḥ aśaktaiḥ pūritam tadā
verses.translation: "Here is that exquisite bow, oh, Brahman, which is held as a time-honoured bow by the lineage of Janaka kings, and with which even the highly forceful kings are rendered inefficient to take aim with it, previously...

glosses.meaning: to take aim [with it,] not, efficient ones

verses.devanagari:
नैतत् सुरगणाः सर्वे सासुरा न च राक्षसाः |
गंधर्वयक्षप्रवराः सकिन्नरमहोरगाः
क्व गतिर्मानुषाणां च धनुषोऽस्य प्रपूरणे |
आरोपणे समायोगे वेपने तोलनेऽपि वा
verses.iast:
na etat sura gaṇāḥ sarve sa asurā na ca rākṣasāḥ |
gandharva yakṣa pravarāḥ sa kinnara mahoragāḥ
kva gatiḥ mānuṣāṇām ca dhanuṣo asya prapūraṇe |
āropaṇe samāyoge vepane tolane api vā
verses.translation: "None in all the assemblages of gods, inclusive of demigods, demons, gandharva-s, yaksha-s, kinnaraa-s, or reptilian demigods, is capable enough to take aim with this bow and all are rendered incapable... and then, in brandishing this bow for a proper grip, or in bracing its bowstring to the other end, or in twitching the bowstring for its tautness, or in placing the arrow on bowstring at a proper place for a proper stretchability, or even in taking a good aim with it... what will be that capability of one from among humans...

glosses.meaning: this one - the bow to take aim
in weighing or, balancing [in brandishing for a proper grip]
in twitching the bowstring [for its tautness]
by what, course [capability,] among humans, even.

verses.devanagari:
तदेतद्धनुषां श्रेष्ठमानीतं मुनिपुंगव |
दर्शयैतन्महाभाग अनयो राजपुत्रयोः
verses.iast:
tat etat dhanuṣām śreṣṭham ānītam munipuṅgava |
darśaya etat mahābhāga anayoḥ rāja putrayoḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, eminent-saint, such as it is, this nonpareil bow among all bows is brought in, and oh, highly fortunate sage Vishvamitra, let this be displayed to those two princes..." Thus Janaka said to Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: that [such as it is,] this, among bows, nonpareil one
this one, to two of them, king's, sons [princes,] you may show.

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रः सरामस्तु श्रुत्वा जनकभाषितम् |
वत्स राम धनुः पश्य इति राघवमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
viśvāmitraḥ sa rāmaḥ tu śrutvā janaka bhāṣitam |
vatsa rāma dhanuḥ paśya iti rāghavam abravīt
verses.translation: Vishvamitra on listening the sentence of Janaka along with Rama, on his part said to Raghava, "oh, boy Rama... you may see the bow..."

glosses.meaning: oh boy, Rama, bow, you see

verses.devanagari:
महर्षेर्वचनाद्रामो यत्र तिष्ठति तद्धनुः |
मंजूषां तामपावृत्य दृष्ट्वा धनुरथाब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
maharṣeḥ vacanāt rāmo yatra tiṣṭhati tat dhanuḥ |
mañjūṣām tām apāvṛtya dṛṣṭvā dhanuḥ atha abravīt
verses.translation: Upon the word of the great sage Vishvamitra, Rama on unclosing the lid of that strongbox, wherein that bow is ensconced, saw the bow and said.

glosses.meaning: that, bow, wherein, it is ensconced

verses.devanagari:
इदं धनुर्वरं ब्रह्मन् संस्पृशामीह पाणिना |
यत्नवांश्च भविष्यामि तोलने पूरणेऽपि वा
verses.iast:
idam dhanurvaram brahman saṃspṛśāmi iha pāṇinā |
yatnavān ca bhaviṣyāmi tolane pūraṇe api vā
verses.translation: "Now I wish to get the feel of this supreme bow, oh, Brahman, and I shall try to brandish it, or even try to take aim with it...

glosses.meaning: with hand [hands-on,] I will touch - I wish to get the feel of
in brandishing, in taking aim, even, or
a trier, I wish to become, even.

verses.devanagari:
बाढमित्येव तं राजा मुनिश्च समभाषत |
लीलया स धनुर्मध्ये जग्राह वचनान्मुनेः
verses.iast:
bāḍham iti eva tam rājā muniḥ ca samabhāṣata |
līlayā sa dhanur madhye jagrāha vacanāt muneḥ
verses.translation: "All Right!" said the saint and king to Rama in chorus, and Rama upon the word of the sage grasping it at the middle handgrip playfully grabbed the bow.

glosses.meaning: to him - to Rama, equally [in chorus,] said
he Rama, upon the word, of sage
bow, at its middle [grasping at middle handgrip of bow,] playfully, grabbed.

verses.devanagari:
पश्यतां नृसहस्राणां बहूनां रघुनंदनः |
आरोपयत्स धर्मात्मा सलीलमिव तद्धनुः
verses.iast:
paśyatām nṛ sahasrāṇām bahūnām raghunandanaḥ |
āropayat sa dharmātmā sa līlam iva tat dhanuḥ
verses.translation: While many thousands of men are witnessing that right-minded Rama the legatee of Raghu stringed the bow effortlessly.
notes: A bow has a definite height and it is a measure of length, from the ages even up to the age Kautilya, who gave many accounts for weights and measures, in his 'Artha Shaastra' a Penguin re-publication. Four aratni-s cubits are one dhanu, a bow-length, where one aratni is 18 inches, thus a bow-length is 6 feet and above, taking the standard size of archer as a six-footer and a little above. The bow's height is the height of the archer plus one measure of his head's height, as the upper end has to tower the archer's head. That being so, this bow belongs to Shiva and its height must be placed more than the human measure of 6 feet, and then it must be some 8 to 10 feet. And 'Rama is no crane-legged boy, as hisphysique is said to be of 'medium' size, and then how a boy of, say of 4, 41/2 feet, could catch the upper end of 8-10 feet bow to bend it...' is the objection. An archer has to stand the bow on ground, clutch its lower end under big toe, and with one hand, he has to bend it, while with the other he catches the bowstring to string the other end. He is not supposed to handle it like a holdall or a briefcase. For this objection it is said in a way that the poet is using the adjective mahātmā to Rama, ' an unfathomable one with an equally unfathomable soul... inasmuch as his duty is concerned...' The minute he touched the bow, it became a spongy stick and it listened to him and bent as he wished. Other way round, Rama is an ambidextrous archer and furthered is his skill by his possession of some divine missiles as given by Vishvamitra. Hence, his dexterity is now multiplied and he can handle any divine or human bow 'effortlessly...'

glosses.meaning: virtue souled one [right-minded,] he, that Raghu's, legatee - Rama
many, people, thousands of, while witnessing
stringed the bow to take aim.

verses.devanagari:
आरोपयित्वा मौर्वीं च पूरयामास वीर्यवान् |
तद्बभंज धनुर्मध्ये नरश्रेष्ठो महायशाः
verses.iast:
āropayitvā maur.hvīm ca pūrayāmāsa vīryavān |
tat babhañja dhanur madhye naraśreṣṭho mahāyaśāḥ
verses.translation: Further, that dextrous one has stringed that bow with bowstring and started to stretch it up to his ear to examine its tautness, but that glorious one who is foremost among men, Rama, broke that bow medially.
notes: The bow is not broken by itself because of its oldness or dryness, but let us blame Rama for breaking it, as with any other toy which children are apt to damage in their playing. He stretched the bowstring so long until it broke. Neither his mother nor father available here. Otherwise, a 'moral class' would have chanced on him for braking articles in neighbour's houses. The bow is broken in the middle, not at either end, but at handgrip. This shows the strength of his palm to handgrip.

glosses.meaning: started to stretch the bowstring [up to his ear to see its tautness]
glorious one, the one best among men

verses.devanagari:
तस्य शब्दो महानासीन्निर्घातसमनिःस्वनः |
भूमिकंपश्च सुमहान् पर्वतस्येव दीर्यतः
verses.iast:
tasya śabdo mahān āsīt nir.hghāta sama niḥsvanaḥ |
bhūmi kampaḥ ca sumahān parvatasya iva dīryataḥ
verses.translation: Then there bechanced an explosive explosion when the bow is broken, like the explosiveness of down plunging thunder, and the earth is tremulously tremulous, as it happens when a mountain is exploding.
notes: We can write more words for the above sound as, 'Dhaam, Dhiim, Phut, and DiSkuu...' etc., as long as thesaurus permit. But all that will be nonsensical. An ear-splitting sound has come but it is "OM" the auspicious sonus prima grata, produced once upon a time by Shiva's drum, in order to emanate words through maheśvara sūtrāṇi, which were unintelligible even for the sages like Sanaka, Sananda, Sanat Kumaara et al., and which were deciphered by Nandi, the Holy Bull vehicle of Shiva, to those sages. Here it is Shiva's bow and name of Shiva and all letters that attaches to Him are śaṃ, śaṃkara, śambhava, are peace-making letters, as codified in AUM namaH shambhave ca mayo bhave ca namaH sha~Nkaraaya ca mayaskaraaya ca namaH shivaaya ca shivataraaya ca | - rudram - soma suukta - yajur Hence the real sound of Om is audible and it is ear-splitting for ordinary audience, since ordinary people cannot possibly face realities, and it is a regularly audible sound for the other four who have not swooned. By the way, it will be impossible for us to listen the chanting of Veda-s, even in these days, in any Vedic school for at least half an hour, as our ears are untuned to their ghana pāṭha or jaṭa or other sorts of chanting. We feel stranded in some audio studio with fully loaded sound FX.

And the pacemaker Rama lifted the bow of the peacemaker Shiva, where the bow itself is "Om". The legendary Indian bow is composed of three parts, unlike Robin Hood's single-piece bow. The lower bowing part, upper bowing part combined by a grip handle, and the bowstring. The three pieces are comparable to the three letters syllabified "Om" - a u ma, where a is upper bowing piece of bow, u, the lower end, and ma, the bowstring. The painters usually paint this bow-breaking scene, where Rama will be still handling the upper end in his hand, while the lower part will be falling, and the bowstring will be still dangling onto the upper end. The upper part of bow is a and this a is Vishnu akāra artho viṣṇuḥ, and the dangling bowstring is ma Goddess Lakshmi, loka mātā mā ramā mangala devatā, dangling on the Supreme Person through thick and thin, and the detached-un-detached lower end is u, Lakshmana, or any other adherer. A lengthy account of this trilogy is provided in Aranya Kanda, Ch. 11, first verse.

And the pacemaker Rama is marrying the world with peace, by stringing the bowstring of peacemaker's bow, and it is not a mere marriage of some prince charming, with a charmy princess. Thus, this sound is the initial impact, impetus, brunt, or whatever, for universal peace, and that way this marriage attains a legendary significance in peace process, though by force.

glosses.meaning: of mountain, exploding, like [as it happens]

verses.devanagari:
निपेतुश्च नराः सर्वे तेन शब्देन मोहिताः |
व्रजयित्वा मुनिवरं राजानं तौ च राघवौ
verses.iast:
nipetuḥ ca narāḥ sarve tena śabdena mohitāḥ |
vrajayitvā muni varam rājānam tau ca rāghavau
verses.translation: Bewildered by that raucous caused by the breakage of bow, all the people swooned, except for that eminent-saint Vishvamitra, king Janaka, and those two Raghava-s, namely Rama and Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: saint eminent Vishvamitra, king Janaka, those two, also, Raghava-s

verses.devanagari:
प्रत्याश्वस्तो जने तस्मिन् राजा विगतसाध्वसः |
उवाच प्रांजलिर्वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञो मुनिपुंगवम्
verses.iast:
prati āśvasto jane tasmin rājā vigata sādhvasaḥ |
uvāca prāñjaliḥ vākyam vākyajño munipuṅgavam
verses.translation: While the people are being reaccustomed after their undergoing the shock, at that moment that sententious king Janaka, whose discomfiture has completely departed by now has said this to the eminent-saint Vishvamitra with a reverent palm-fold.

verses.devanagari:
भगवन् दृष्टवीर्यो मे रामो दशरथात्मजः |
अत्यद्भुतमचिन्त्यं चातर्कितमिदं मया
verses.iast:
bhagavan dṛṣṭa vīryo me rāmo daśaratha ātmajaḥ |
ati adbhutam acintyam ca atarkitam idam mayā
verses.translation: "Oh, godly sage, the gallantry of Dasharatha's Rama is evidently seen... and the whys of this boy and wherefores of his stringing that massive bow are unimaginable to me! More so, humans lifting it! How so? This is an unhoped-for incident for me, besides, breaking it! This a is highly wondrous experience for me...

glosses.meaning: has seen, gallantry - his gallantry is seen

verses.devanagari:
जनकानां कुले कीर्तिमाहरिष्यति मे सुता |
सीता भर्तारमासाद्य रामं दशरथात्मजम्
verses.iast:
janakānām kule kīrtim āhariṣyati me sutā |
sītā bhartāram āsādya rāmam daśaratha ātmajam
verses.translation: "My daughter Seetha on getting Dasharatha's Rama as her husband, she will bring celebrity to the lineage of Janaka-s...
notes: This verse explains the advantageous status of Seetha than Rama in her birth and brought up. mama sutā 'my daughter...' though I have not given her a physical birth, she is godsend to me, and I brought her up as a rarest of rare daughter with all the endowments of Janaka-s lineage which are impeccable... hence she is more than my physical daughter...' sītā 'a furrow... born a furrow, an unusual non-uterine birth than the uterine birth of Rama from his mother Kausalya... hence Seetha has a plus point... daśaratha ātmajam 'Dasharatha's, son...' a wooable bridegroom... because he is Rama ramayate iti rāma 'makes others delightful...' besides this, the saying about an eligible bridegroom is there: kanyā varayate rūpam mātā vittam pitā śrutam bāndhavāḥ śīlam iccanti sūpa annām itare janāḥ 'a bride cherishes charming mien, a prince-charming, rather... mother of the bridegroom wishes to have money through him... bridegroom's father wants him to be a wise one in dealings with his new wife and old parents... and bridegroom's relatives require of him good demeanour... and other people wish to have dough of cooked pulse-gram, marriage-feasts, rather...' so also my daughter will cherish this boy as his looks are like that of a prince-charming... and the money for his mother, scholarly attitude to his father, good demeanour and feasts etc., to friends and relatives, all he can afford... and on āsādya reaching Rama... my daughter brings kīrti 'celebrity' to our lineage, which is in singularly unique... because kīrti is said in singular number, it will be singularly unique... hence let this boy not negate my proposal as my daughter has many plus points...'

verses.devanagari:
मम सत्या प्रतिज्ञा सा वीर्यशुल्केति कौशिक |
सीता प्राणैर्बहुमता देया रामाय मे सुता
verses.iast:
mama satyā pratijñā sā vīrya śulkā iti kauśika |
sītā prāṇaiḥ bahumatā deyā rāmāya me sutā
verses.translation: "Oh, Kaushika, my commitment that she is the bounty of bravery has also come true... and my daughter Seetha who is nurtured well than my own lives is a worthy bride for Rama...

glosses.meaning: to Rama, giveable - worthy to be given.

verses.devanagari:
भवतोऽनुमते ब्रह्मन् शीघ्रं गच्छंतु मंत्रिणः |
मम कौशिक भद्रं ते अयोध्यां त्वरिता रथैः
verses.iast:
bhavato anumate brahman śīghram gacchantu mantriṇaḥ |
mama kauśika bhadram te ayodhyām tvaritā rathaiḥ
verses.translation: "Should you give consent, oh, Brahman, my ministers will be hastened to speedily go to Ayodhya in chariots, oh, Kaushika, let safeness betide you, and one and all by this matrimony...
notes: Annex: 'This boy appears to be straight from the shoulder type, and he may now say boyishly, 'no, no, I just wanted to see and feel the bow, but that poor old bow is broken in my hand, but I have never said that I will marry your daughter without the consent of my father... and I am supposed to marry whomever my father ties down my neck...' knowing him to be such, I want to send proposals to Dasharatha at Ayodhya, that too if you say yes...'

glosses.meaning: by you, in consent - with your consent
by chariots, to Ayodhya, quickly, they go

verses.devanagari:
राजानं प्रश्रितैर्वाक्यैरानयंतु पुरं मम |
प्रदानं वीर्यशुक्लायाः कथयंतु च सर्वशः
verses.iast:
rājānam praśritaiḥ vākyaiḥ ānayantu puram mama |
pradānam vīrya śuklāyāḥ kathayantu ca sarvaśaḥ
verses.translation: "With their observant submissions those ministers will narrate in detail about the sincere endowment of Seetha as bravery's bounty to Rama, and they will lead king Dasharatha into my city that observantly...

glosses.meaning: sincere, endowment of such a girl in marriage
in detail, [they the ministers] will narrate
to my, city, they will lead him in.

verses.devanagari:
मुनिगुप्तौ च काकुत्स्थौ कथयंतु नृपाय वै |
प्रीतियुक्तं तु राजानमानयंतु सुशीघ्रगाः
verses.iast:
muni guptau ca kākutsthau kathayantu nṛpāya vai |
prīti yuktam tu rājānam ānayantu su śīghra gāḥ
verses.translation: "Those ministers will also tell the king Dasharatha that both the Kakutstha-s, Rama and Lakshmana, are under the aegis of saint Vishvamitra, and thus gladdening that king they will expeditiously usher in king Dasharatha for marriage..." So said Janaka to Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: by saint [Vishvamitra,] as shrouded - under the aegis of, also
glad, along with [making glad, gladdening him

verses.devanagari:
कौशिकश्च तथेत्याह राजा चाभाष्य मंत्रिणः |
अयोध्यां प्रेषयामास धर्मात्मा कृतशासनान् |
यथावृत्तं समाख्यातुमानेतुं च नृपं तथा
verses.iast:
kauśikaḥ ca tathā iti āha rājā ca ābhāṣya mantriṇaḥ |
ayodhyām preṣayāmāsa dharmātmā kṛta śāsanān |
yathā vṛttam samākhyātum ānetum ca nṛpam tathā
verses.translation: Vishvamitra said, "so be it," and then that right-minded king Janaka on consulting with his ministers started to send his ministers, plenipotentiaries, to Ayodhya to inform Dasharatha in detail as to what has happened, and likewise to bring him to Mithila.

glosses.meaning: Kaushika - Vishvamitra, also, so be it, thus, said
as, has happened, in full detail, to tell
king Dasharatha, to bring in, also
one who is made, to implement orders [ministers plenipotentiary]
